This paper presents an innovative approach to IoT network security that combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with advanced deep learning approaches, encompassing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Transformers. In this research, we investigate the potential of PCA for dimensionality reduction and feature selection within IoT network data. By simplifying data complexity, PCA aids in uncovering critical features and patterns contributing to network anomalies. Advanced deep learning models, such as GANs for generating synthetic data and Transformers for sequence modeling, are harnessed to construct anomaly detection systems capable of identifying irregularities in real-time IoT data streams. Our approach is rigorously evaluated on a comprehensive dataset collected from diverse IoT devices and networks. The results underscore the efficacy of the PCA and deep learning-based anomaly detection model, leveraging GANs and Transformers, in accurately and efficiently unmasking anomalies in IoT network traffic. Through extensive experiments and evaluations, we underscore substantial advancements over traditional security methods. This research significantly enhances IoT network security by presenting a sophisticated, data-driven anomaly detection system adaptable to the dynamic and evolving nature of IoT environments. As the IoT landscape continues to expand, our approach offers a crucial solution to safeguard against the ever-evolving threat of network anomalies.

articleTitle: Synthetic Data Generation and Handling Data Imbalance for Mobile Financial Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: It is always challenging to get the financial transaction data due to the data privacy issue. This research paper presents an approach for detecting financial fraud using machine learning techniques by augmenting the data. The proposed method leverages the power of synthetic data generation techniques to create large volumes of realistic data that can be used to train and evaluate machine learning models. Specifically, here Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are used to generate synthetic data that closely resembles real-world data while preserving its statistical properties. The generated data are highly imbalanced. So measures are taken to handle the data imbalance. Moreover, the noises present in the data are also removed by utilizing edited nearest neighbourhood techniques. Then these data are used to train and test several machine learning models, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and logistic regression. Our results show that using synthetic data can significantly improve the performance of machine learning models for fraud detection, achieving high levels of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Moreover, our approach is shown to be robust to imbalanced datasets, which is a common challenge in fraud detection.

articleTitle: Implementing Machine Learning Techniques to Optimize Near-Field Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With applications ranging from consumer electronics to medical equipment, electric cars, and industrial automation, near-field wireless power transfer, or WPT, has become a promising new technology. This abstract offers a unique method for optimizing near-field WPT using machine learning approaches, which offers notable improvements in user experience, safety, efficiency, and flexibility. Three important machine learning techniques are introduced by the suggested method: Dynamic Power Control using Neural Networks (DPC-NN), Predictive User Behavior Modeling (PUBM), and Reinforcement Learning for Resonance Tuning (RLRT). To guarantee the best possible power transfer efficiency, RLRT continually adjusts the system's resonance frequency. By predicting user behavior, PUBM helps the system be ready for charging events in advance. To ensure safe and effective operation, DPC-NN dynamically regulates power supply. A glaring benefit may be shown when comparing the suggested approach with six conventional approaches. In terms of effectiveness, security, user happiness, interference reduction, predictive maintenance, dependability, flexibility, and environmental impact, the suggested approach continuously performs better. These findings demonstrate how machine learning may revolutionize near-field WPT and spur efficiency and innovation in a range of sectors.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques For Signal Processing On Spherical Manifolds In Near-Field Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Improvements in deep learning have benefited signal processing on spherical surfaces in particular. This work addresses deep learning for close-range spherical surface signal processing. Traditional signal processing algorithms may struggle to handle complex data on spherical surfaces. Deep learning has the potential to close this gap. Our deep learning in signal processing examination begins with its principles, difficulties, and accomplishments. The article goes on to illustrate how spherical geometry influences data encoding and signal processing, underscoring the need for understanding signal processing on spherical manifolds. The research emphasises the need for cutting-edge solutions to tackle non-Euclidean data representation challenges quickly. We are experimenting with several deep learning architectures for spherical manifold data. Among these architectures are attention mechanisms, GNNs, CNNs, and so on. Integrating these models with spherical data layers and methodologies should allow for a thorough evaluation of their ability to detect complex close-range patterns.Deep learning algorithms increase near-field signal processing on spherical manifolds in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and resilience, according to the results. Deep learning architectures for curved spherical data processing are advanced in this work. This objective necessitates research on its theoretical underpinnings, existing approaches, and practical applications. These unique and adaptable data management solutions provide remarkable data management on spherical manifolds for near-field applications. Their data management systems are more precise and trustworthy than earlier ones.

articleTitle: A Multicriteria Aware Multipath Routing Method to Increase the QoS for Future 6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The optimal solution of creating a communications network in isolated places is still a challenging task. Establishing end-to-end connectivity via mobile ad-hoc networks (MANETs) is a better solution for the above issue. However, the limitation of the mobility of nodes and battery resources between the overlay and mobile ad-hoc network protocols is still a challenge for trustable wireless connections. Therefore, this paper presented a routing scheme named Mobility and Energy consumption aware multipath routing (MEMR) in mobile ad-hoc networks. The proposed routing scheme provides reliable communication with stable route and high lifetime routes to support efficient data transmission in the network. For this purpose, it uses a multicriteria decision-making approach to select the intermediate nodes with the highest energy and lowest mobility for selecting the optimal route. The obtained results indicate that the proposed routing method can significantly improve the overall network performance and deliver packets with acceptable throughput. At the same time, it reduces the energy consumption of the nodes compared with the conventional MP-OLSRv2 routing protocol.

articleTitle: Sleep Disorder Prediction with AI User Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Health is the most precious thing for living beings than anything else. Everyone wants to live more and healthy enough to do what they love. Sleep is a way which helps us refresh ourselves. Most of the time we just need a good amount of sleep to restore our mental and physical health. But in some cases, we are not able to get proper sleep for various reasons which could possibly lead to a kind of sleep disorder. But the awareness of this is very less among people. They simply ignore this, which leads to the problem becoming more worse. To avoid that, many AI models have been developed to detect sleep disorders in early stages. Sleep disorders are of two types, which are apnea and insomnia. These both are detected using various tests with EEG, EMG, EOG, ECG, etc. sensors on patient during sleep. But this could be costly and time taking process. So we suggest a simple AI model, which takes simple parameters like age, sleep duration, sleep quality, etc as inputs and gives a prediction whether the person is prone to have any sleep disorder, based on which the person can visit a doctor accordingly. This is a simple and fast method to simply check the possibility.

articleTitle: Bio-Inspired Algorithms for Self-Healing and Adaptation in Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Bio-inspired algorithms are becoming more and more popular as a way to solve challenging problems in sensor networks wit in the framework of self-healing and adaptation. This study offers a novel approach to enhancing sensor network performance using Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Genetic Algorithms (GA). To demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed strategy, we compare it against six industry standard methodologies. The presented work majorly focusing on resource use, accuracy, efficiency, speed, and reliability. Hence, the results of the experiment show that the recommended technique is better in many important areas. It performs better than traditional methods in several areas, including as resource use, efficiency, and accuracy and reliability. In addition to efficiently managing energy, the PSO module encourages self-organization. The ACO enhances routing and fault tolerance. The GA optimizes node placement and recovery mechanisms to function in everchanging network conditions. The suggested technique offers a comprehensive answer to the problem of sensor network selfhealing and adaptation, making it an excellent option for a wide range of practical uses.

articleTitle: Optimal Transmission Expansion Planning in Deregulated Power Markets Using AI-Enhanced Cost-Based Pricing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Transmission expansion planning plays a critical role in ensuring the reliability and efficiency of power systems in deregulated markets. In such markets, optimal expansion planning becomes complex due to uncertainties in electricity demand, generation technologies, and market dynamics. This research paper reviews and analyses some research papers that focus on the utilization of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced cost-based pricing strategies for achieving optimal transmission expansion planning in deregulated power markets. The paper categorizes and evaluates these studies based on methodologies, case studies, AI techniques employed, and their contributions to the field tested on radial 5-bus system. The synthesis of these works highlights the growing significance of AI techniques in addressing the intricate challenges posed by transmission expansion planning within deregulated power markets.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Transport Layer Protocols in Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The transport layer is a vital network layer component responsible for ensuring the reliable delivery of data between two points in a communication network. The delivery layer protocols in cellular networks are essential for facilitating the efficient transmission of information between mobile devices and the network. Evaluating the performance of shipping layer protocols in cell networks is crucial to ensure an optimum and efficient communication system. This review examines the current status of research on evaluating the performance of transport layer protocols in mobile networks. The main objective of the performance evaluation of delivery layer protocols is to assess and analyze the quality of service offered by these protocols. The key metrics utilized to assess the overall efficacy of these protocols include bandwidth, latency, and variability in latency, and packet loss. These characteristics directly impact the uninterrupted transmission of data and the overall user experience. An important difficulty in assessing transport layer protocols in cellular networks is the ever-changing network conditions. Due to the portability of devices, community resources such as bandwidth and signal power could be more consistent, resulting in difficulties in achieving reliable outcomes. Furthermore, increasing diverse mobile devices and networks adds complexity to assessing performance. Various strategies and methodologies are employed to assess the overall performance of transport layer protocols in cellular networks.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Efficiency of Computational Genetic Epidemiology using Advanced Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The incorporation of cutting-edge computational methodologies and machine learning strategies and genetic epidemiology has made tremendous strides in recent years. To speed up and refine genetic epidemiology studies, we present a new method called “Enhancing the efficiency of computational genetic epidemiology using Advanced Methods” (ECEGEM), which utilizes modern computational methods and innovative technologies. The three primary methods used by ECEGEM are Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Logistic Regression, and the determination of the Polygenic Risk Score (PRS). Using PCA, we can ensure that the underlying substructure of the population is not confounding genetic connections. Through its ability to predict the association between genetic variations and illness outcomes, Logistic Regression sheds light on the hereditary nature of a variety of conditions. Individuals may get more accurate risk estimates using PRS computation, which considers their unique genetic makeup. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, Naive Bayes, kNearest Neighbors, and Decision Trees were some of the six classic approaches we used to evaluate ECEGEM against. It was shown that ECEGEM was much more accurate and precise than the conventional approaches. This highlights the promise of sophisticated computational methods for improving the accuracy of illness risk assessment and association research. Because of its ability to take into consideration population stratification and provide more accurate modeling and risk assessment, ECEGEM has been shown to be an effective tool in genetic epidemiology. Personalized medicine and the understanding of the genetic basis of complicated illnesses will benefit greatly from the use of cutting-edge technologies and machine learning as the field develops.

articleTitle: Automated Malware Classification Using Deep Learning Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Ingenious applications of millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar for simultaneous monitoring of several targets are possible. It's conceivable, however, that the radar unit itself may malfunction. Improving mmWave radar detection while keeping accurate data classification is difficult. One of the main obstacles to fully capitalizing on mmWave sensing is the time and effort required to construct a model that is compatible with tracking and sensing objectives. Manually annotating mmWave data is time-consuming and often requires subject knowledge since radar frames relate to big events. In this piece, we cover the basics of using a camera for labeling and monitoring in mmWave radar training. A rough sketch of the framework was made during the investigation stage. The effectiveness of the suggested technique is assessed in comparison to other approaches with similar objectives. The conceptual framework has been confirmed by experiments in a range of real-world scenarios. The resulting multi-object tracking system makes use of millimeter wave (mmWave) technology. This technology is unique in that it can tell the difference between a runner, a runner who has stumbled, and a walker. The experiment's results demonstrate that a camera's guided tagging may be used to reliably train a radar model. This trained model continuously exhibits outstanding classification accuracy across a broad variety of examples, not just the ones it was trained on. This paper provides a foundation for further study of hybrid monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Data Mining Techniques In Bioinformatics Enhanced by HPC and AI Convergence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: High-Performance Computing (HPC) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have come together to usher in a new age of data mining in the field of bioinformatics. Using high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI), this research presents a suggested strategy for improving data mining techniques and then evaluates it alongside six more conventional approaches. Discovering latent patterns in high-dimensional biological data is the goal of the proposed technique, which combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Random Forest (RF). The suggested technique consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in our comparisons, including in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. These performance criteria are essential for effective data mining in bioinformatics, and the system's shown equilibrium between them is rather impressive. The suggested strategy also drastically decreases execution time, which is a crucial aspect in effectively managing large-scale biological information. Our findings highlight the need for AI-driven data mining methods in the field of bioinformatics. The application of PCA offers dimensionality reduction, assisting in feature selection and boosting model performance. When it comes to classifying and ranking the value of features, RF provides ensemble learning capabilities, whereas CNNs excel at extracting complicated patterns from pictures and sequences. The suggested technique is holistic in nature, drawing on the advantages of several algorithms to improve data mining and provide a complete service to the field of biological research. Our results show that the suggested approach has considerable potential to further bioinformatics studies and applications. It helps scientists speed up drug development, improve the accuracy of diagnostics, and unearth new biological insights. In addition, the faster execution time suggests better use of computer resources, which is useful for making decisions and analyses in the life sciences and healthcare in real time.

articleTitle: AquaticSafe Sentinel: An Edge-Based IoT-Powered Predictive System for Continuous Dissolved Oxygen Surveillance in Aquaculture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Aquaculture stands as a flourishing industry, serving as a significant financial resource for many. However, it encounters various challenges such as environmental degradation and disease outbreaks. Consequently, maintaining water quality in aquaculture systems becomes imperative. Dissolved oxygen (DO), a key indicator of oxygen availability for fish respiration, emerges as a crucial measure of water quality. In this research, we propose AquaticSafe Sentinel, an innovative IoT-backed predictive system designed for edge-based continuous monitoring of DO and real-time alerting in aquaculture. Our two-phase framework utilizes both edge computing and cloud computing to swiftly and reliably predict DO levels based on environmental and biological characteristics. Phase one involves making ensemble forecasts of DO levels at the cloud layer using a combination of three machine learning approaches, namely Linear Regression, Random Forest, and AdaBoost. Then phase two involves employing the results of Linear Regression at the edge of the network to make real-time decisions about DO levels, and triggering alerts if necessary. Subsequently, the system awaits a more refined conclusion from the combination technique at the cloud layer. We conduct a comparative analysis with various baseline methods, demonstrating that our framework surpasses them in terms of prediction accuracy and computing efficiency. Additionally, we illustrate how our framework effectively minimizes false alerts, achieving a balance between speed and accuracy to deliver timely solutions.

articleTitle: DynaFog: A Dynamic Task Offloading Framework for IoT-Based Fog Computing Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper explores the complexities of task offloading in a dynamic fog computing network, where multihop Internet of Things (IoT) access points (APs) support the connectivity between IoT devices and fog computing nodes. The suggested DynaFog framework is organised around key elements in the context of IoT architectures based on fog computing. These components include the selection of fog nodes with skill, the optimization of paths for effective offloading, and the best decision-making about local or remote task computation. We carefully formulated the task offloading problem over a multi-hop communication link by considering an integer linear program (ILP) in order to handle this intricate scenario. Owing to the non-convexity of the possible solution set, a greedy approach-driven heuristic strategy has been proposed to efficiently navigate the problem space. The technique for the solution incorporates a holistic viewpoint that covers multi-hop routing, energy utilization, delay, and dynamic network characteristics, particularly with regard to utilization of link and fog controllers' capacity. Our experimental results validate the effectiveness of the suggested strategy, demonstrating a noteworthy decrease in average delay and energy usage in comparison to benchmarks.

articleTitle: Exploration on the Application of Speech Recognition Model in Power Marketing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With the rapid development of the national power industry, smart grids have become a major direction of current power system reform and technological innovation. This article adopted a speech recognition model used in the power industry, which is characterized by the ability to preprocess speech data. Voice data includes voice data unique to the power industry and voice data with regional characteristics. This article separated and extracted speech features, and trained them to obtain a speech recognition system suitable for power system applications. The speech recognition model can automatically recognize the speech of people from different regions, thereby saving a lot of human resources in the process of power marketing. Before using the speech recognition model, the industrial rating was 3 points, and after using the speech recognition model, the industrial rating was 6 points. The quality of power marketing services was improved. The application of speech recognition models in power marketing in this article is an important guarantee for ensuring the stability and safe operation of the power grid.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation Based on LSTM-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Deep learning methods have demonstrated potential in estimating the health state of lithium batteries, which is essential for safety management. Yet, they often struggle to capture long-term dependencies and global correlations within battery capacity sequences. To address this challenge, a fused LSTM-Transformer approach for lithium battery health state estimation is proposed. the excellent sequence modelling capability of LSTM enables it to effectively capture the long-term dependence of battery performance evolution over time and adapt to pattern changes in different time scales, while the Transformer model achieves excellent global correlation capture through the self-attention mechanism. to understand the charging and discharging behaviour of batteries in a more global perspective. This integration allows the models to surpass the limitations inherent in using a single model and improves the ability to model the dynamic complexity of battery systems. Additionally, experimental results using a public dataset confirm that the method introduced in this paper offers a more thorough and precise evaluation of battery health compared to alternative deep learning artifacts.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Privacy Preservation Approach in Data Mining Using Noise Additive Model in Continuous and Multi-Dimensional Data Set
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Data mining raises serious privacy issues. Privacypreserving data mining for multi-dimensional data sets, however, results in significant data loss, information leakage. An innovative method called Multidimensional Noise Additive Model (MNAM), which improves cluster identification and privacy while reducing information leakage, is suggested in this study. Anonymization technique that incorporates aggregation is applied in multidimensional data sets which leads to the reduction of information leakage and enhances the privacy. The domain-specific range of the subspaces are taken into consideration when performing noise addition. The MNAM method considers Euclidian distances among the neighboring clusters. Then, anonymized subspaces are subjected to random noise inside the subspace bounds to improve cluster detection and minimize data loss. Conventional algorithms fail to discover the types of clusters in datasets, MNAM is able to detect the majority of the original dataset clusters. Benchmark datasets are used to test MNAM, and the results demonstrate that MNAM can locate 85% of the underlying dataset clusters, in contrast to existing approaches that fail to locate any clusters. MNAM improves privacy by 65% while reducing data leakage by 60%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Robotic Automation In Industries Using Industrial Informatics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This research investigates the field of industrial informatics to suggest a novel method, EnhancedRoboAI, with the potential to radically alter the way robotic automation is used in manufacturing. Insights into the expanding need for improved automation capabilities in today's industrial environment are provided in the introduction, with the limits of traditional approaches and the promise of industrial informatics for resolving these issues being highlighted. EnhancedRoboAI is compared to six well-established conventional approaches (AutoIndustro, IndustriaNet, AutomateWorks, RoboTechPro, IndustriAutoPro, and AutoSolutionsInc.) in this study. Factors such as precision, velocity, the capacity to deal with complicated data, flexibility, learning speed, and resource use are used to assess performance. EnhancedRoboAI demonstrated higher performance across all parameters in the exhaustive assessment process, yielding convincing findings. For instance, EnhancedRoboAI improved accuracy by 13%, speed by 16%, and resource use by 7% when compared to AutoIndustro. By outperforming IndustriaNet by 15%, EnhancedRoboAI demonstrates its flexibility as a solution for the dynamic demands of today's manufacturing environments. Based on the findings of this research, a new age of industrial automation has begun, with the implementation of EnhancedRoboAI promising to take efficiency, responsiveness, and productivity to new heights.

articleTitle: Secure Communication Protocols for Enhancing Privacy in 5G Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The 5G mobile network is innovative in providing low-latency conversation services. However, this new era brings massive issues around privacy and safety. With the boom in linked and Internet of Things (IoT) gadgets, the danger of touchy information being accessed through unauthorized activities will increase. Cozy communication protocols are essential to decorating privacy in 5G mobile networks. The protocols use advanced encryption and authentication techniques to protect records transmitted over the net. Further, they deploy at-ease channels among devices to prevent interception and manipulation of the use of malicious actors. One of the number one protocols for securing conversation in 5G networks is the 5G Authentication and Key settlement. This protocol employs mutual authentication and a significant era of the equipment and the network, ensuring that the handiest prison devices can accurately enter the network and that the transmitted records are encrypted and protected.

articleTitle: Enhanced Accuracy Model for Edge Computing and IoT Leveraging Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper delves into the significant role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the realms of Big Data, Internet of Everything (IoE), and Cloud Computing. It analyzes AI's influence on these domains, exploring its applications, challenges, and future prospects. The paper highlights AI's pivotal role in shaping the technological landscape, driving innovation, and addressing complex data-related tasks across diverse sectors. The escalating integration of AI in these sectors and its specific applications are thoroughly addressed. Additionally, the paper introduces a predictive model for industrial pump failure rates, highlighting the synergy between Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Everything(IoE).

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Blockchain for Enhanced Transparency in Government Public Records
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With more things done online, citizens have never wanted government data to be more available and dependable. This paper proposes a solution using blockchain and powerful algorithms. The recommended approach uses blockchain's immutability and safety, machine learning to discover outliers, and NLP to organize data. This coordinated strategy automates and opens government records to increase data quality, accessibility, and speed. Several tests and performance assessments compared the recommended solution to the traditional record-keeping method. Finding anomalies is faster using machine learning anomaly detection and natural language processing record sorting. This ensures data accuracy and clarity in real time. Spreading blockchain keeps documents secure and unchangeable. This makes changing difficult for those who shouldn't. The study found that the proposed strategy might improve public record management. It improves transparency, a crucial trait for responsible leadership, in a powerful, safe, and automated way using blockchain technology and cutting-edge algorithms.

articleTitle: Ai-Siot Hybrid Architecture for Seamless Integration of IoT in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: IoT technology allows many devices to be connected, creating Smart cities (SCs). Because gadgets from different manufacturers are heterogeneous, control and interaction present problems. These devices generate truckloads of data, but only practical analysis can produce intelligent services. This paper presents a new service architecture: the AISIoT hybrid, which combines various IoT devices and provides them with intelligent services. It relies on semantic and AI technologies to integrate diverse devices. AI enables rapid data analysis and exact service supply decisions in varied settings. The paper shows how the AI-SIoT architecture is implemented in several use scenarios. The opportunities and constraints of AI-SIoT deployment in future Smart Cities are also examined.

articleTitle: Ensuring Transparency and Fairness in AI DecisionMaking Processes Influenced by large language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper tackles the essential problem of assuring openness and justice in AI decision-making processes driven by huge language models. While large language models like GPT-3 have shown impressive capabilities, they have also prompted questions of fairness, transparency, and ethics. The “FairTransLing” approach contains features to improve interpretability, bias reduction, fairness evaluation, transparency, regulatory compliance, and real-time monitoring, and is proposed as a solution to these problems. The state-of-the-art and time-tested approaches “Interpret ML,” “Fair ML,” “BERT Viz,” “FairGAN,” “LIME,” and “AIF360” were tested against FairTransLing in great detail. We compared these strategies based on six criteria: improved interpretability, reduced bias, increased fairness, improved transparency and fairness, more regulatory compliance, and continuous monitoring. The suggested strategy performed better than the conventional approaches in every respect. Our results demonstrate that FairTransLing provides a complete approach to increase interpretability, eliminate biases, and measure fairness in AI decision-making. Ethical problems and possible biases are reduced because of its emphasis on openness, regulatory compliance, and real-time monitoring. This study is a major advance toward the transparent and equitable implementation of massive language models used in AI systems.

articleTitle: Remote Patient Health Monitoring with Cardiovascular Illness using the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: COVID-19 epidemic plus the ongoing partial lockdowns make a difficult moment for the critical patients. Even the doctors treating the patients have maximum probability to get infected. Monitoring the patients' pulse rates and oxygen levels has become crucial for the patients. Doctors in these situations rely on patients to measure temporal measurements of vital bodily parameters for therapeutic purposes. Therefore, it is suggested in this work to create a low-cost, effective data logger for remote recording and monitoring of the physiological characteristics of the human body, such as temperature, heart rate, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, etc. Doctors may remotely access patient data via an integrated data logger that is built utilizing an IoT-based cloud server to monitor patients. The sensor data is successfully tested and recorded on the Thing Speak server, and an alerting system using Light emitting diodes (LEDs) and buzzers is created to notify doctors in case of an emergency.

articleTitle: Harnessing Security Improvements Using FaceNet Approach for Face Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In the realm of education technology, the integration of biometric authentication has garnered significant attention for its potential to streamline and enhance traditional attendance management systems. This research explores the development and implementation of a Face Recognition-Based Attendance System (FRBAS) using the state-of-the-art FaceNet technology. FaceNet, renowned for its accuracy and efficiency in facial recognition, serves as the backbone for the proposed system. The Face Recognition-Based Attendance System (FRBAS) leverages FaceNet technology to not only provide a seamless and secure method for recording attendance but also offers a robust solution for identity verification. By harnessing the power of deep learning, the system ensures high accuracy and reliability in recognizing facial features, reducing the chances of errors associated with traditional methods. Additionally, the integration of biometric authentication not only enhances security but also facilitates a more efficient and timely attendance tracking process, promoting a technologically advanced and streamlined educational environment.

articleTitle: Synergistic Fusion of Multi-Contrast Imaging and Computational Image Synthesis for Quadruple Contrast-Enhanced Images and Multi-Map Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Medical imaging has changed a lot since “Synergistic Fusion of Multi-Contrast Imaging and Computational Image Synthesis for Quadruple ContrastEnhanced Images and Multi-Map Generation” came out. This innovative technology might revolutionize diagnostic imaging by providing a complete view of tissue features and enhancing accuracy. This study describes a system that utilizes ultrasound, PET, MRI, and CT data. Better detection is the goal of this technology. This first segment begins a new medical imaging age in which clinicians may view the full patient by combining data from diverse sources. The strategy might increase diagnosis accuracy, treatment focus, and healthcare quality. This research uses cutting-edge deep learning, feature extraction, and fusion techniques. DLESA synthesizes images using convolutional neural networks. Since no one does it by hand, errors are less likely. The Feature Extraction and Fusion Algorithm (FEFA) integrates significant features from several picture approaches to maximize their benefits. CERA and SAEA are essential for picture clarity and line accuracy. Reality reveals that the proposed way performs better than usual. PSNR (13.29%), SSIM (6.98%), CNR (11.61%), and Dice Coefficient (8.54%) have all increased. The technology may be utilized outside of healthcare since it employs science to mix data, learn deep, and extract characteristics. This strategy that integrates multiple disciplines of research might revolutionize how we obtain, analyze, and use information, leading to groundbreaking scientific, technological, and health advances. This novel technology advances diagnostic pictures and data-driven diagnostics, bringing accuracy and comprehension to medical and other disciplines.

articleTitle: Integrating Pretrained CNN and SVM for Improved Lung Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Lung Cancer is nowadays becoming a very common disease and a significant reason for death among Indians. Lung cancer often comes in two different forms: small- cell lung cancer and non-small-cell lung cancer. Among all other factors, Smoking cigarettes is one of the major reasons for lung cancer. The body is severely harmed by lung cancer, which is one of the most prevalent and dangerous cancers today. Therefore, the only method of treating lung cancer that is truly successful is early detection and diagnosis. Many lives would be saved if it should be diagnosed at an early stage. Lung Carcinoma, an uncontrolled malignant tumor characterized by uncontrolled cell growth in lung cells, is the alternative name for lung cancer. The paper aims to classify lung cancer in CT scan images. The greatest imaging technique available for medical use, a CT scan can be difficult for physicians to interpret and use to identify cancer. This paper proposes a technique that uses a hybrid method by combining the Support Vector Machine algorithm with CNN (Convolutional neural network) and gives better accuracy. CT scan images of patients are classified as to what type of lung cancer by using this technique. This technique efficiently classifies the cancer into its types. Using a hybrid model (Support Vector Machine algorithm with CNN technique) is an effective way to correctly identify the stages of lung cancer and pursue more accurate findings.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Machine Learning in Enhancing Agricultural Practices and Food Production
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: As the world's population rises, the agricultural industry must find ways to increase food production while reducing waste and pollution. Machine learning is an AI branch that has recently gained attention as a game-changing tool with the potential to completely alter the agricultural industry. In order to optimize many facets of farming and food production, machine learning is at the forefront of current research and practical applications, as is discussed in this abstract. Precision agriculture is made possible by the combination of machine learning algorithms with cutting-edge sensing technology including remote sensing, IoT devices, and drones. They provide farmers access to actionable insights for better crop management, irrigation, and pest control. Using these methods, we may better anticipate disease outbreaks, allocate resources efficiently, and make more accurate yield predictions. Further, by supporting enhanced resource management, decreasing waste, and minimizing environmental consequences, machine learning approaches contribute to sustainable farming. This presentation also delves into how machine learning may be used to optimize supply chain management, post-harvest processing, and food distribution in addition to detecting and monitoring agricultural diseases. Leveraging machine learning models to evaluate and anticipate market trends and customer preferences might help decrease food waste and guarantee that agricultural goods reach consumers more effectively.Finally, the abstract highlights the need of improved cooperation between academics, farmers, and policymakers when discussing the obstacles and future potential of machine learning in agriculture. Ultimately meeting the rising global food demand while reducing the industry's environmental impact, the use of machine learning in agriculture has the potential to revolutionize the sector.
